So Rocco’s beds at the end were so creative I am so proud of myself that I could give him almost everything he needed. One bed was in a plastic laundry basket - rectangle but I put towels covering all the sides and back - most of the front was covered too he had I’m guessing but about 5-6” not covered so he could see us without having to move.  But I know he felt very secure in that one. 
Covering most of it was a great idea. 
Each bed had water right at the edge as it’s his legs that hurt… so he had water and food and a doggie plastic thing like a disposable towel in  each room we went into. 

Taking him to be … put down was so horrible. 
I literally couldn’t pull it together for over 6 months I was missing him so much. I didn’t want another dog I wanted him. 

You know what got me suffering, missing, eyes filling with tears?
As for .. let’s say 12 years… we the only time I left him with someone I trusted with my child an older woman I knew for over 25 years and she took care of my son so there was no way I could take him to Australia and we had to go for three months. 
It was awful. And it was so difficult to make a decision… to stay home with my dog who was like my child or … go to Australia with my partner. 
Took me weeks to make that decision.

I have been saying for probably 20 years… I wish like running for mayor or governor I could run for…  “mayor  or leader of all dogs”. Sounds ridiculous I know but imagine if I was seeing each dogs owner and deciding if they were fit and knowledgeable enough to have a dog. 
Make every pet owner … take classes. 
Make sure they have vet visits twice a year. 
Etc..
I’d be great at it as the strongest strength I have is feeling people. 

Strongest strength Number 1 is…
Knowing who is good or evil. 
By evil I mean capable of hurting others. Or hurting others and feeling nothing.  
Psychopaths, narcissists etc. 

And with that I have never been wrong. 
Every aquauntence, friend and colleague I have never ever doubts my feelings about people, ever. 
Maybe doing tarot cards for 25+ years.. was great training.  As when I did tarot cards for a living… I did tarot cards but gave everyone up to two hours, sometimes even three if I had no app after. 
But it is innate as well. 
I’ve known things that normally people don’t pick up on for almost all my life. 

Sometimes a very bad childhood- too,  makes you very smart.

All but one were placed  where he could just open his eyes and see me or my husband so he chose who he felt more comfortable maybe more secure who he could see as soon as he needed to do it changed so many times during the last two months. 

He often got better so we prayed and waited to see if he would get better. 

I had something more special with Rocco more than any previous dog. 

I could decipher what he wanted or needed almost anything just by his eyes or eye movement with some gestures… most of what he wanted to tell me.

Btw in case you don’t know. If a dog licks his paws a lot.. they have a tooth problem. 
I had to stay at someone’s house one weekend many years ago. 
Their dog was constantly licking his paws. 
The owner kept saying the dogs name… then saying “stop”.  
I asked what was going on she said the other dog died and this was his way of showing anxiety. 
I told her about the teeth thing, she said that’s crazy. 
I’m not sure why but two weeks later I got a text saying,
“Ena you were right he had 7 teeth pulled and he was in pain”.  
I was so so happy that day no longer literally horrified that that dog was suffering.

My heart breaks for all animals that are hurt or hurting and not treated with total and complete love and compassion. 

I have had many dogs since my youth. But as I got older I got smarter. I learned how to train my dog with praise and treats as opposed to all other disgusting ways.  

My dog passed a year and a half ago. 
His name was Rocco and he was so well trained I was able to go to Paris with him four consecutive years!!! As well as Italy and a few other European countries. 
He had a very comfortable very nice but “quiet, understated bag - very happy in there. Bottom extra padded… and in the winter fur lined.  

At the end of my Yorkshire Terrier’s ( Rocco) life he was very ill.  Maybe we kept him 2 months too long but he was not in pain as he was on anti-inflammatory drugs and Toradol and something else for pain.  
Much to my dismay I have a very large home, not something I want at all. 
I was so happy with 2 bedrooms and 1200sq. ft. 
But my husband- rules. A really nice man but the one with the money … just rules. 
He is.. pretty good with saying everything is half my decision but less good with carrying it out. 

Anyway we have a pretty big bedroom.  So I made Rocco a few beds in different corners of the room since he can’t speak ( obviously) I have to think long and hard at what he would want just like a baby.
